what: Transwell images. Pair A: the block of eight images shown as Invasion in Fig 3F (SHG44 and U373; shNC+NC, shcircEPHB4, MRPS16, shcircEPHB4+MRPS16) is the block shown as Migration in Fig 7C (shNC+NC, shcircEPHB4, YBX1, shcircEPHB4+YBX1). Pair B: the block shown as Invasion in Fig 1D (shNC, shcircEPHB4-1, shcircEPHB4-2) is the block shown as Migration in Fig 2F (shNC, shMRPS16-1, shMRPS16-2).
why: Row labels: one block is 'Invasion', the other 'Migration'. These are separate assays (invasion inserts are Matrigel-coated), so the same field of cells cannot be both. Column labels: the third and fourth columns are MRPS16 overexpression in Fig 3 but YBX1 overexpression in Fig 7, and circEPHB4 knockdown in Fig 1 but MRPS16 knockdown in Fig 2. The captions also describe different experiments (Fig 3: cells 'transfected with shNC, shcircEPHB4-2 or/and MRPS16 overexpression construct'; Fig 7: cells 'transduced with AAV-shNC, AAV-shcircEPHB4 or/and AAV-YBX1'). Source: panel labels and captions.

what: Fig 7 wound-healing assay. The 'Vector, 48 h' image in panel A and the 'Vector, 48 h' image in panel B are the same image.
why: Panel headers: A is T98G, B is U87MG, two different glioblastoma cell lines. Methods: each line got its own vector control ('The cells were designated as U87MG-NID2, U87MG-vector, T98G-NID2, T98G-vector'), so this is not one control shared by two treatments: a field of T98G-vector cells cannot also be a field of U87MG-vector cells. The 0 h Vector images of the two panels are different from each other, as expected for two wells. Source: panel headers, Methods.

what: Not cell culture: scanning electron micrographs in Fig 1. The SEM image under (E) is the mirror image of the SEM image under (D).
why: Caption: '(C-G) represents the particle size determination by zeta sizer and surface morphology determination by SEM for (C) exosomes (D) Exo-PAC (E) Exo-5-FU (F) FA-Exo-PAC, and (G) FA-Exo-5-FU.' D is the paclitaxel-loaded preparation and E the 5-fluorouracil-loaded one: two different samples. Imaging a different sample cannot give the same particles in mirror image; mirroring is an editing step. Source: caption.

what: Not cell culture: rat wound photographs in Fig 5. Panels A, B and C are one photograph. B is A shown 1.2x smaller; C is A stretched about 25% vertically and cropped. The wound starts at the same pixel in all three and is cut progressively shorter from its right end (3.3, 2.2, 0.9 cm by the ruler), and the fur around it is smoothed in B and C.
why: Caption: 'Representative photographs of dorsal full-thickness skin wounds showing healing progression at day 3 (A), day 7 (B), and day 14 (C) post-injury.' Methods: 'Macroscopic wound assessment was performed on days 3, 7, and 14 after injury. Digital photographs were obtained ...'. Photographs taken 4 and 11 days apart cannot share the same glove position, ruler position, table speck and wound outline. Source: caption, Methods.

what: Fig 9E, the 200X images under the colony plates. The right part of the si-CDH1-A549 image shows the same cells as the left part of the Ctrl-A549 image: the two fields overlap.
why: Column labels: 'Ctrl-A549' and 'si-CDH1-A549'. Caption: '(E and F) Colony formation assay images (E) and quantified data (F) demonstrating a marked decrease in the number of colonies formed by si-CDH1-A549 and si-CDH2-A549 cells.' Control and CDH1-knockdown cells grow in separate dishes, so one microscope field cannot contain cells of both. Source: column labels, caption.

what: Fig 5 transwell invasion of CaSki cells. The lower left of image (b) shows the same cells as the upper right of image (a): the two fields overlap.
why: Caption: 'Invasion of CaSki cells was measured by transwell assay in (a) blank, (b) negative, and (c) Ezrin siRNA groups.' Blank (untransfected) and negative-control siRNA are separate groups in separate inserts, and the bar chart gives each its own count, so one field of cells cannot belong to both. Source: caption, bar chart.
